text: The proposed boundary fixes only half the stated defect. The ledger identifies BOTH ambient-state access and library panicking as wrong, but v1 explicitly retained the panic in the library; making workspace_drift nonpanicking merely moves that responsibility into its callers. Preferred shape: thread a drift handler such as fn(&str), implemented in tests/common/cdo.rs and invoked at the three check points, so the test-owned handler selects warning versus panic. That preserves return types, early termination and warning suppression without the library owning either decision. If the real requirement is only 'no ambiently selected panic', say so explicitly rather than claiming failure moved out of the library.
evidence: Correct, and adopted in full -- the handler is also smaller than the DriftPolicy enum I proposed (a function pointer, no enum, no match). The design now states the requirement explicitly as BOTH halves, because round 1's point was precisely that v1 met one while the ledger claimed two.

text: Three direct callers, but SEVEN public entry points: three path-based wrappers, three _on wrappers, and run_cdo_semantic_audit_on_raw (:2355-2408, :2570-2721), which has a real test caller at tests/program_resolve_harness.rs:5073. 'Three entry points' understates the signature changes.
evidence: Verified and corrected. A8 now enumerates all seven and names the raw wrapper's test caller. My pre-claim scope check counted CALL SITES correctly and then wrote 'entry points', which is a different thing -- the measurement was right and the wording was not.

text: No inspected test expects the drift panic or captures the warning suppression, and the library has no direct drift unit test. A7 asserts only the panic; add an explicit negative assertion that no WARNING: line is emitted under enforcement.
evidence: Adopted as A5 and folded into A9's discrimination. The suppression is real -- the assert! at :356 preempts the eprintln! at :361 -- and it is exactly the kind of behaviour that survives a refactor by accident and breaks silently later.

text: A5 asserted only that catch_unwind returned Err and inferred the eprintln! was unreachable. That proves the current body, not a regression: moving the print above the assert, or deleting it, both keep the test green while breaking the behaviour.
evidence: Reproduced both counterexamples as D3 and D4. Replaced the inference with captured stderr from a child process (Command::env). D3 now fails 101 on print-before-assert; D4 fails 101 on a deleted print; both byte-restored under sha256 ac551ed9fca3f141. Round 2 re-raised it: stdout and stderr were merged, so a println! passed the stderr assertion. Streams now separate; D5 fails 101 on that mutation. Round 3 re-raised it a second time: the gated assertion matched only the exact sentinel-bearing line, so eprintln!("WARNING: {msg:?}") broke suppression while dodging it. Fixed by rejecting the WARNING: PREFIX on both streams; D7 confirms (exit 101, byte-restored). astra has not re-reviewed that fix -- final_rounds is spent.

text: unsafe std::env::set_var in the lib tests is not made safe by a mutex shared between two tests: it does not serialize libtest thread pool, it clears an inherited value instead of restoring it, and cleanup is skipped if the call under test panics.
evidence: The lib tests no longer touch the environment at all; the half that needs ENFORCE_CDO_WS=1 set runs in a child process via Command::env from the harness. Zero unsafe blocks remain in the diff.

text: Only the trigger audit's check point was ever driven with drift; the semantic and event check points are reached only by CDO-gated tests where the stamp matches, so deleting on_drift there, or re-adding an env assert there, would stay green.
evidence: PARTIALLY fixed: the probe also calls run_cdo_event_audit and counts handler calls (1, then 2); D12: removing the event check point's on_drift fails it, exit 101. DEFERRED: the semantic check point. CORRECTED REASON (both stand-ins, round 3): a fixture DOES exist (tests/fixtures/semantic-golden, harness:1178). The real obstacle is that driving the semantic audit on a real fixture calls merge_deanon_map, merging that fixture's sites into the developer's local, gitignored cdo-deanon-map.json.
